 1499/2023 Channakeshava. K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/
3 Keshava and pillion riders M.Madhu and B.Anji fell down on the Road, sustained grievous injuries. Due to the head injury suffered by M.Madhu, he died on the spot. 
 3. It is the further case of the Petitioners in MVC No.836/2023 that, immediately deceased M.Madhu was taken to Govt. Hospital, Palamner, conducted Postmortem and body was handed over to the petitioners. So far they have spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards, conveyance,

 5. It is the further case of the Petitioners in MVC No.1499/2023 that, soon after the accident K.Channakeshava was shifted to Government Hospital,
Palamner, provided first aid and thereafter petitioner shifted  SCCH - 25 7 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &

 6. The accident was caused due to the rash and negligent act of the Driver of the Mahindra Pickup Goods Carriage vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-TT-3260. The Jurisdictional Gangavaram Police have registered the case Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/

 7. In response to the summons, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels but the respondent No.2 alone filed written statement in all the cases. 
 8. The objections of the Respondent No.2 in all the cases:
 It has denied the entire averments made in the claim petitions except admitting the issuance of policy in respect of Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-39-TT-3260 in favour of the 1st respondent. There was delay of one day in lodging the complaint. There was non joinder of necessary parties to the petition. It has denied the manner of accident,
involvement of the vehicle in the accident. Further denied the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased  SCCH - 25 9 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023 M.Madhu. The accident was caused solely due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.AP-39- Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/
6 RN-7194. Further contended that the TWO WHEELER IS DESIGNED FOR TWO PERSONS ONLY AND NOT FOR TOO MANY PERSONS. There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) of MV Act. The rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-RN-7194 did not have valid DL as on the date of accident, he rode the two wheeler motorcycle with 2 pillion riders in utter violation of the traffic Rules and also the provisions of the MV Act and Rules. It has further denied the age, income, occupation, medical  SCCH - 25 10 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &

this court has framed the following issues:

Issue No.1 Issue No.2 Issue No.3 Issue No.4  MVC No.836/2023 In the In the In the As per final  affirmative affirmative affirmative Order  MVC No.842/2023 In the In the As per final --  affirmative affirmative order  MVC No.1499/2023 In the In the As per final --  affirmative affirmative order  REASONS  13. Issue No.2 in MVC No.836/2023 and Issue  No.1 in MVC No.842/2023 & 1499/2023:- 
 In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the Driver of the Mahindra Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-TT-3260,

10 the Petitioner No.2 in MVC No.836/2023 got examined as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of her chief examination and got marked Exs.P.1 to 6. During the cross examination of PW.1, she has admitted that three of them were wearing helmet. The rider Channakeshava had DL. They have also got examined one eye witness as PW.5 and got marked 1  SCCH - 25 15 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023 document and filed affidavit in lieu of his chief examination. During the cross examination of PW.5, he has stated that Srinivas and he were standing at the accident spot to go to Hugni Gate from his house and the spot of accident was about 50ft away from where he was standing. The Petitioner in MVC No.842/2023 & the petitioner in MVC No.1499/2023 got examined themselves as Pws.2 & 3 and filed affidavit in lieu of their chief examinations. During the cross examination of PW.2, he has admitted that there were Three members in the bike and he was sitting in the middle of the motorcycle. They were going in the speed of 30km/hr. During the cross examination of PW.3, he has admitted that he was riding the bike on the date of accident. Three of them were going on the bike. Venkatesh, father of the deceased M.Madhu gave the complaint on the next day of accident. He was riding the bike in the speed of 30km/hr. The respondent No.2 has contended that the petitioners and the deceased  SCCH - 25 16 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023 Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/
11 were not wearing the helmet at the time of accident. The Two Wheeler is designed for Two Persons only and not for too many persons. It has got examined its official as RW.1. 
During the cross examination of RW.1, he has admitted that the policy was valid to the insured Mahindra Pickup Goods vehicle bearing No.AP-39-TT-3260. They have not written any letter to the insured. Further admitted that none of the police documents show that the injured and deceased were not wearing the helmet. The charge sheet filed against the Goods vehicle and it is falsely filed. They have not challenged the charge sheet. Further admitted that the deceased and injured are third parties with respect to insurance. The third party risk is covered and since the injured and deceased lost control and fell it can not be covered. 
 14. All the petitioners have produced the police documents i.e., FIR with complaint, spot sketch, inquest mahazar, PM report, MV report and charge sheet as per  SCCH - 25 17 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023 Exs.P.1 to 6. On perusal of documents it is clear that the accident occurred on 23.01.2023 at about 18.20 and the FIR was registered on the next day at about 9.00am. The complaint was given by Venkatesh M. Father of deceased M.Madhu. The Sketch shows that the accident occurred on the NH of Bangalore - Chittoor. The Inquest Mahazar conducted on 21.01.2023 from 10.00am to 24.01.2023 Channakeshava. K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/
12 12.30. PM report shows that M.Madhu died due to vital organ injuries. As per the IMV report, the Mahindra and Mahindra Bolero Pickup got damaged to its front bumper on LH side, Left hand fender got damaged, left hand head lamp broken and Left hand side mirror broken and front left hand wheel damaged. After investigation charge sheet is filed against the driver of the Mahindra Bolero Pick up vehicle. Other than the police documents, none of the other parties have produced any other documents contrary to these. 
 SCCH - 25 18 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023  The counsel for the Petitioner has relied upon the following decisions:
 (i) MFA No.4237/2015 : Kum. Ranjitha Vs. Reliance Gen. Ins. Co. ltd. ,and Anr.
 Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka  has held that only because the rider of the Two  wheeler did not have DL and was carrying more  than Two Pillion riders, such violation of traffic  law itself cannot be considered as contributory  negligence unless insurance company leads  additional evidence to prove the same.
 (ii) MFA No.202001/2018 : Mallanna Vs.
Mahadevappa and Anr.
 'Unless the insurance company leads evidence to  show that the violation of the statutory provision  of Sec.128 of MV Act itself was the cause for the  accident, contributory negligence cannot be  considered'.
 (iii) MFA No.101144/2020: Ananda Vs. Arjun and Anr. 
 Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka  has held that not wearing the helmet itself does  not show the negligence. 
Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/
13  (iv) MFA No.2179/2018: The Reliance General Ins.
Co. Ltd., Vs. Smt. Shobha and Ors.
 Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka  has held that non wearing helmet is not a ground  to deny compensation.
 SCCH - 25 19 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023  The counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied upon the following decisions: 
 (i) 2010 ACJ 1316 : National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs.
S.Chitra and Ors.
 Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Madras has  held that the very conduct of the persons carrying  more than Two persons in motorcycle amounts to  negligence. 
 (ii) (2009) 13 Supreme Court Cases 654 : Raja Rani and Ors. Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., and Ors. 
 Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has  held that claimants were negligent in not  observing parked vehicle and determined the  contributory negligence at 50%. 
 However, the respondents have not produced any document to show that the very fact of the petitioners and the deceased Triple riding in the motorcycle and not wearing helmet led to the accident. Instead the documents on record show that the Lorry has hit the Two wheeler from behind. Therefore, on the basis of all these documents is clear that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence and rash driving by the driver of the Mahendra Pickup Goods Carriage vehicle bearing No.AP-39-TT-3260.
 SCCH - 25 20 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023 Nothing is brought on record by any of the parties to show there was any kind of negligence on the part of the rider of Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/
14 the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-RN-7194.
Accordingly, issue No.2 in MVC No.836/2023 and Issue No.1 in MVC No.842/2023 & MVC No.1499/2023 are held in the affirmative. 
 15. Issue No.1 in MVC No.836/2023: 
 It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the father and Petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased - M.Madhu. The Petitioners to prove their relationship have examined the 2nd Petitioner as PW.1. 
PW.1 has specifically spoken about this relationship in her chief-examination. Apart from that, to prove the relationship, the Petitioners have produced notarized copy of their Aadhar cards and also produced the Aadhar Card of the deceased, Notarized copy of Ration Card of family of petitioners as per Exs.P.8 & 9. In the Aadhar Card of the deceased, his father's name is mentioned as M.Venkatesh. 
 SCCH - 25 21 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 & 
 1499/2023 In the Aadhar Card of the petitioner No.1 his father's name is shown as Late M.Krishnappa and in the Aadhar Card of the petitioner No.2 her husband's name is shown as M.Venkatesh who is the petitioner No.1 and father of the deceased. In the Ration Card the head of the family's name is shown as M.Saradamma who is the petitioner No.2 and also mentioned the name of the petitioner No.1 and the name of the deceased. In the Inquest at Ex.P.3 the name of the petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are shown as father and mother. 
Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/
15 These documents are public documents and they have got initial presumptive value under law. These documents have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents. The Respondents have not produced any contrary documents to dispute and rebut the contents of documents produced by the Petitioners. As such, there are no reasons to discard the oral and documentary evidence produced by the Petitioners. Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and the documents, this court is of  SCCH - 25 22 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023 the opinion that the Petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are the father and mother of the deceased M.Madhu. Accordingly, Issue No.1 in MVC No.836/2023 is held in the affirmative. 
 16. Issue No.3 in MVC No.836/2023:
 PW.1 has specifically spoken before this court that due to the untimely death of the deceased, they have lost their loving affectionate Son. While discussing the issue No.2, this Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the due to actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle the alleged accident occurred. Therefore, under these circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation. 
 Age and Income of the deceased:
 17. In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced the Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.8. 
Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/
16 As per this document his birth year is 10.03.2005 and the accident occurred on 23.01.2023. As such, the deceased  SCCH - 25 23 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023 was 17 years as on the date of accident and from this, it is very clear that as on the date of accident, the deceased was a minor. Further, the petitioners have stated that, the deceased was working as Mason and earning Rs.25,000/-
per month. In this regard they have not examined any witness nor produced any documents to prove the same. 
Moreover at the time of accident he was minor but PW.1 has stated that the deceased had studied only till 5th Std.,
and was working as a Mason. The accident occurred in the year 2023. Therefore, considering the evidence of PW.1,
this Tribunal deems it fit to fix the notional income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/- per month. 
 (i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:-
 As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation,
appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 18. In the instant case, the deceased has Father and Mother 44 & 40  SCCH - 25 24 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023 years old. PW.1 in her cross-examination admitted that her husband is not working, he has some problems with his leg. As such petitioners are depending on the income of the deceased. Therefore, both petitioners father and mother are Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/
17 considered as the dependents of the deceased. 
 . 
 18. As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects. As mentioned above, since the deceased was under 40 years age slab,
40% future prospects is to be added to his monthly income. So Rs.6,400/- (Rs.16,000/- X 40% = Rs.6,400/-)
should be added to his monthly salary of Rs.16,000/- then it comes to Rs.22,400/- per month. As per the Sarala Verma case, if the deceased is a bachelor, then 1/2 of his income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses, balance comes to Rs.11,200/-. Therefore, the  SCCH - 25 25 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023 total loss of dependency would be Rs.24,19,200/-
(Rs.11,200/- X 18 x 12) = Rs.24,19,200/-).
 (ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:-
 In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs.
Nanuram (2018) 18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed  "Consortium" is a compendious term, which  encompasses spousal consortium, parental  consortium and filial consortium. The right to  consortium would include the company, care, help,
 comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the  deceased, which is a loss to his family. With respect  to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with  the deceased spouse".
Channakeshava.K vs Thoti Nagendra Babu on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110324970/
18  19. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd.
Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021)
11 SCC 780.
 20. The Petitioners are the father and mother of the deceased. They have to live remaining part of their life in  SCCH - 25 26 MVC Nos.836/2023  842/2023 &
 1499/2023 the absence of their young son. The loss of a young son full of hopes for the future can never be suitably compensated to the parents. However, petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.48,000/-each (10% addition after every three years from 2017 as per Pranaysethi Judgment) i.e., Rs.96,000/-
under the head of loss of consortium. 
 (iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL  EXPENSES AND LOSS OF ESTATE:-
 In so far as the funeral and transportation expenses are concerned, the Petitioner has contended that she has spent a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
